p: Before you head in, a quick team chat goes a long way. Agree who'll watch the clock, who'll keep hold of found objects, and when you'll ask for a hint. Then, once the door shuts, search everything before trying to solve anything. Escape rooms reward teams who gather all the pieces first and then work out how they fit, rather than getting stuck on one locked box for ten minutes.

Milton Keynes is brilliant for groups because it's so easy to get to. The town sits right by the M1, and Milton Keynes Central station has fast trains from London and the north, with Xscape and the main shopping area reachable on foot or by a short bus ride. That makes it a top meeting point for friends spread across the region.

Milton Keynes has a lot more to it than people expect. The city's famous Concrete Cows are a quirky local icon, and Campbell Park, right behind the centre, offers sculpture trails and sweeping views. Willen Lake is great for lakeside walks and watersports, and the network of redways, the shared paths for cyclists and walkers, makes getting about on two wheels a pleasure. History lovers shouldn't miss Bletchley Park, home of the wartime codebreakers, which feels like a natural follow-up to an hour of cracking codes yourself. MK Gallery and Milton Keynes Theatre, both near Campbell Park, add a dose of culture, and younger children will love Gulliver's Land theme park on the edge of town.
